analysis.session_summary: The window was a USD-supportive, risk-on session: DXY closed +0.423% at 102.146 and USD strength was +0.225%, while AUD (+0.261%) and NZD (+0.099%) outperformed. EUR was the weakest major (-0.293%), dragging EUR/USD down 57.9 pips. The main US event, CB Consumer Confidence, beat significantly (91.7 vs 81.2) but triggered an inverted USD dip of 0.052%, suggesting crowded USD longs. Most intraday legs had no clear catalyst, with the tape dominated by flow and event-positioning ahead of the heavy calendar.

themes.theme: USD strength with commodity FX outperformance
themes.evidence: USD +0.225%, AUD +0.261%, NZD +0.099%; AUD/USD +2.5 pips and AUD/CHF +0.284%.
EUR -0.293% against majors; EUR/USD -57.9 pips, EUR/CHF -25.0 pips, EUR/AUD -0.555%.

themes.theme: Inverted USD reaction to strong US data
themes.evidence: CB Consumer Confidence beat 91.7 vs 81.2 but USD weakened 0.052%; Gold/USD +0.128% and AUD/NZD +0.04%.

currency_drivers.USD: USD closed at its best (+0.225%) despite the inverted CB Consumer Confidence reaction; no other US catalyst explains it.
currency_drivers.EUR: EUR had no clear catalyst and was the weakest major, closing down 0.293%.
currency_drivers.JPY: JPY had no clear catalyst and finished lower against all majors.
currency_drivers.GBP: GBP had no catalyst and traded near session lows, closing down 0.127%.
currency_drivers.AUD: AUD had no domestic catalyst; early selling was rejected and it became the strongest major.
currency_drivers.CAD: CAD had no catalyst; an early 0.12% bid was rejected, giving back 89%.
currency_drivers.CHF: CHF had no catalyst and held a tight range, ending nearly flat at -0.023%.
currency_drivers.NZD: NZD had no domestic catalyst; it held its range and closed 0.099% firmer.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: The pair's three legs—a 51.2-pip decline, a 14.8-pip bounce, and a 19.8-pip slide—summed to a 57.9-pip loss with no leg attributed to a clear catalyst.

polarity_reads.read: The CB Consumer Confidence beat produced USD weakness (inverted), suggesting long-USD positioning was used for profit-taking on good news.

scenarios.name: Commodity FX extension
scenarios.thesis: AUD/NZD and CAD benefit from domestic event risk while EUR lags; USD stays firm but loses to commodity currencies.
triggers: AUD CPI y/y prints at or above 4.2%
RBNZ OCR delivers 3.00% with hawkish tone
BOC hikes to 2.50% and signals more
scenarios.invalidation: Dovish RBNZ/BOC or a risk-off shock reverses AUD/NZD and USD/CAD.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR closed near session low; repeat of today's range if USD holds.
AUD selling was rejected earlier; CPI beat extends recovery.
BOC hike supports CAD, reversing USD/CAD's 36.2-pip gain.

scenarios.name: USD range consolidation
scenarios.thesis: DXY closed at its best and major pairs are stretched; the event calendar encourages two-way flow within today's ranges.
triggers: AUD CPI meets 0.7% m/m and 4.2% y/y
RBNZ delivers expected 3.00% OCR without new hawkish signals
GBP Budget contains no major fiscal surprise
scenarios.invalidation: A break of DXY 102.146 high or a strong US data surprise.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD closed near low of range, likely mean revert to mid-range.
USD/JPY closed at 0.99 of range; upside limited without fresh catalyst.
AUD/NZD closed at 0.98 of range; both AUD and NZD event risk caps extension.

scenarios.name: USD correction / crowded long unwind
scenarios.thesis: Inverted CB Consumer Confidence reaction signals crowding; high-impact events may trigger USD profit-taking, especially vs EUR and GBP.
triggers: AUD CPI above forecast sparks commodity rally
BOC hawkish enough to support CAD
scenarios.invalidation: Strong US data or risk-off headlines reassert USD safe-haven bid.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD close at 0.01 of range leaves room for short-covering.
GBP Budget positive shock can unwind GBP's 0.127% decline.
Inverted USD reaction implies USD long reduction; USD/JPY closed at 0.99 high.

risks.risk: AUD CPI and RBNZ OCR may cause sharp AUD/NZD repositioning.
risks.why_it_matters: AUD/NZD is most sensitive to CB Consumer Confidence at 2.4 sigma and closed at 0.98 of its 43.8-pip range.

risks.risk: GBP Budget release could move GBP pairs sharply.
risks.why_it_matters: GBP closed down 0.127% and had no catalyst; a fiscal surprise can dominate.
USD/CAD closed at 0.98 of its range after a 36.2-pip gain; BOC is expected to hike to 2.50%.

risks.risk: Geopolitical headlines from Iran and US-Canada tariffs remain live.
risks.why_it_matters: Brent and risk pairs reacted to Iran Supreme Leader; VIX fell 11.9 points.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: The coming window is event-heavy: AUD CPI and RBNZ OCR can extend or reverse today's commodity-FX bid; GBP Budget and BOC decision are the main re-pricing risks for GBP and CAD.
